Triage (R+89, triage seat, session `session_019kDRpB7D2XzVzkaLp57T5D`): **`pm:queue`** · `priority:p2` · `domain:spec` · type **Bug**.

**Lands in:** `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts:543` `translateAction` (and the `globalActions` branch) — overlay `description`, and each `params[i]` matched by `name` with `field` fallback (the same collection rule `checkActionParams` uses) for `label` / `helpText` / `placeholder` / `options`. Not clause ②: the keys are already declared by `TranslationItemSchema` and already validated by `validateTranslationReferences`; the resolver simply fails to apply them — declared ≠ enforced, restored. p2: a translated button opening an untranslated parameter dialog, on a real deployment (`objectstack-ai/duly`, zh-CN).

Family: #14253 (three surfaces with no key at all — a schema expansion, in flight under the maintainer's directive); this card is the resolver half for keys that already exist and should land independently, ⛔ not folded into #14253's PR.

Size/model suggestion: S, `sonnet`/`opus`; one test per newly-overlaid key.

Premise re-read at `a3d5724c8`: `git show origin/main:packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts | grep -n -E "confirmText|successMessage|resultDialog|params"` → `translateAction`'s overlay reads `label` / `confirmText` (462) / `successMessage` (546-547) / `resultDialog` (500-511); the only `params` overlay in the file is the BULK-action branch (613-626), none for `translateAction`; `description` has no action-level overlay (the 123 hit is the object-level fallback comment in `translation.zod.ts`). - No Zod schema, validator or key changes: `translation.zod.ts` untouched, `validate-translation-references.ts` untouched, `ActionSchema` untouched — the dispatch's stop condition was not tripped. Accept/reject behaviour of every schema: unchanged. ✓

Exactly the ruling. ✓
- Spelling: action-param hint is `helpText` (the schema declares it and aliases `help`/`hint`/`tooltip` onto it; the bulk-param surface is the reverse); the resolver reads `helpText` and a pin asserts no `help` key leaks onto an action param. ✓
- `options`: authored side is an array of `{ label, value }`, translation side is a `value → label` map ⇒ matched on `String(opt.value)`, untranslated entries returned as the same object — the shape `translateObject` already resolves for field options. ✓
- Identity contract kept: `params` returns the SAME array when nothing matched and `translateAction` then writes no `params` key (mirrors `translateBulkActionDefs`' `paramsChanged` pattern); a bundle key naming an undeclared param is ignored (the walk is over declared params; the linter already reports it). Both pinned. ✓
- Public surface (the clause-② reason): `ActionLike` gains `description?: string` and `params?: ActionParamLike[]`; new exported `ActionParamLike`; `api-surface/system.json` and `export-origins/system.json` each +1 name, regenerated by the generators (`check:api-surface`, `check:export-origins`, `check:generated` all green on the head). `translateAction`'s exported signature does not move. Assignability judged on `origin/main`: `ActionSchema.description` is `I18nLabelSchema` (string | inline locale map) exactly as `ActionSchema.label` is, and `ActionLike.label?: string` already carries that same narrowing (a resolver answers with one locale's string) — so `description?: string` follows the house precedent rather than introducing a new one; `ActionParamLike` carries an index signature and loosely typed `options`, so parsed `ActionParam`s assign. The only non-test callers outside spec reach `translateAction` through `translateMetadataDocument(metaType, item, …)` in `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` (:3083, :3324, :9228) with loosely typed items — no consumer type edit needed; CI's `Type Check · workspace` / `consumer gates` are the final reading before the flip. ✓
- Liveness ledger: `packages/spec/liveness/translation.json` already asserted `params` LIVE for both `_actions` and `globalActions` groups — this PR makes that row true; no ledger edit owed. Noted. ✓

**② Semver / changeset** — `@objectstack/spec: patch`, customer-facing text without issue ids, fix-shaped prose naming what now renders. The type additions are optional members plus a helper interface, additive; under this repo's launch-window convention (breaking ships as `minor`) a `patch` for an additive-type bug fix is consistent, and the card is `type: Bug`. Accepted as `patch`. ✓
